result.target_topic: 2024 Process Node Manufacturing Status and Roadmap Changes
result.target_summary: As of the end of 2024, most products were manufactured using the Intel 7 node, while high-volume production of the Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes was shifted to Ireland. The company canceled the productization of Intel 20A to focus on the improved Intel 18A node, which is expected to enter high-volume production in 2025.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
D050 (2023) details factory operations, ramping new process technologies, and supply chain capacity. D049 (2024) details the status of specific process nodes (Intel 7, 4, 3) and their high-volume manufacturing locations (Arizona, Israel, Ireland). Both focus on the operational execution and status of manufacturing nodes.

Both disclosures discuss capital-intensive manufacturing, facility/equipment distribution, and the transition to advanced lithography (EUV) requiring significant investment. D050 highlights supply chain/minimizing disruptions in 2023, while D052 in 2024 details the EUV transition and capex split (55% facility, 45% equipment) driven by this new technology.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD utilizes TSMC, GLOBALFOUNDRIES, UMC, and Samsung for wafer production and IC manufacturing for its HPC, FPGA, and Adaptive SoC products, specifically noting GF's role for 12 nm and 14 nm nodes and multiple foundries for programmable logic devices.
comparisons.comparison: This comparison contrasts Intel's vertically integrated manufacturing approach with AMD's fabless model. Intel's disclosure details its own manufacturing operations, including the use of facilities in Arizona, Israel, and Ireland for its Intel 7, 4, and 3 nodes. In contrast, AMD explicitly states that it utilizes third-party foundries, specifically TSMC, GLOBALFOUNDRIES, UMC, and Samsung, for the production of wafers and ICs for its HPC, FPGA, and Adaptive SoC products, rather than operating its own wafer fabs.

sentences.text: As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.

We utilize Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (TSMC) for the production of wafers for our HPC, FPGA and Adaptive SoC products and GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (GF), with respect to wafer purchases for our HPC products at the 12 nm and 14 nm technology nodes.
Additionally, we utilize TSMC, United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) and Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. for the production of our ICs in the form of programmable logic devices.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is on track for volume production of 1-gamma DRAM using EUV lithography in calendar 2025 and has begun volume production of its Micron G9 NAND node.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron explicitly reference the adoption of EUV lithography as a key manufacturing milestone for 2024. Intel reports that it successfully ramped its Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes using EUV lithography and shifted high-volume production to Ireland. Similarly, Micron states that its 1-gamma DRAM pilot production using EUV lithography is progressing well with volume production targeted for 2025. Both disclosures highlight the transition to and ramp of EUV-based process nodes as a critical operational update.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company began volume production of 232-layer Micron G8 NAND in 2022 and Micron G9 NAND in 2024, which are ramping in high volume and will increase in mix through 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific progress in ramping new process nodes into high-volume production during the fiscal year. Intel reports successfully ramping Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes in 2024. Micron similarly reports beginning volume production of its Micron G9 NAND node in 2024, noting that both its G8 and G9 nodes are ramping in high volume. This reflects a shared industry trend of introducing and scaling advanced nodes in the same period, although the specific technologies (logic vs. memory) and nodes differ.

In 2024, we began volume production of Micron G9 NAND, representative of the industry's ninth-generation 3D NAND node.
Micron G8 and G9 NAND nodes are ramping in high volume and will become an increasing portion of our mix through 2025.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fabless manufacturing strategy and cost benefits
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA utilizes a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, employing partners for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging to avoid significant costs and risks associated with owning manufacturing operations. This approach allows the company to focus resources on product design, quality assurance, marketing, and customer support.
comparisons.comparison: This comparison highlights the fundamental difference in manufacturing strategy between Intel and NVIDIA. Intel's disclosure focuses on its internal manufacturing capabilities, describing the ramp and production of its proprietary Intel 7, 4, 3, and 18A nodes in its own fabs. Conversely, NVIDIA describes its fabless strategy, which relies entirely on partnering with key suppliers for all phases of manufacturing, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging, allowing it to avoid the costs and risks of owning manufacturing operations.

sentences.text: As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.

We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ and partner with key suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.
Additionally, we can avoid many of the significant costs and risks associated with owning and operating manufacturing operations.
